summary: Multi-panel dashboard filters snap back to previous time range after retention compaction
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report that dashboards with multiple panels (different queries / route filters) revert their selected time range and panel-level filters to an earlier range after a background retention compaction sweep completes. This appears as a UI "snapback": a user changes the global time range to a recent window (e.g. last 30m), adjusts a panel-level route filter, the panels render correctly, then 20–40s later the global time range and some panel filters revert to the previous snapshot (typically the previously cached 6h window) and several panels show stale tracehook links.

Impact:
- Affects NovaDocs dedicated org (production, us-east) with multiple active dashboards.
- Users lose recently-applied time ranges for live troubleshooting; trace links in affected panels point to pre-compaction runIds that no longer exist in the retention index.
- Workaround is manual re-select of time range and refresh; interrupts on-call investigation and causes longer mean time to resolution for customers.

Environment:
- Prod (dedicated pool) - us-east; org id: org-novadocs-73
- Console version: web-2026.03.10
- Retention compaction job schedule: daily rolling compaction; this issue reproduced immediately following a compaction window triggered for heavy-cardinality tables.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Log into NovaDocs org in us-east.
2) Open dashboard "Service Health — multi-pane" (contains 6 panels, mixed live and aggregated queries).
3) Set global time range to "Last 30 minutes" and toggle panel B route filter to route:analytics-42.
4) Observe panels render with up-to-date metrics and tracehook links.
5) Wait 20–60 seconds.
6) Observe: global time range snaps back to "Last 6 hours" and panel B's filter resets to route:analytics-9; tracehook links update to older runIds and some links 404.

Expected behavior:
- Dashboard retains user-applied global time range and panel filters until user changes them.
- Tracehook links remain bound to the query snapshot used to render the panel and should not revert when compaction background tasks run.

Actual behavior:
- UI reverts to prior cached time range and some panel-level filters are overwritten. Tracehook links reflect the older snapshot and some 404 when the index is compacted and records pruned.

Logs / evidence:
- Browser console logs collected (attached) show a subsequent websocket event "dashboard:refresh_snapshot" with payload referencing snapshot_id: snap-20260313-2100 before the user action.
- Ingest service logs show compaction job started at 2026-03-13T21:00:12Z for table:events_v2-cardinality-high and finished at 2026-03-13T21:00:35Z.
- Query-router logs contain a 200 response for initial queries, then a second identical query issued by the UI with header X-Dashboard-Snapshot: snap-20260313-1200 (older snapshot) at 2026-03-13T21:00:38Z.
- Customer-provided screencast timestamped 2026-03-13T21:00:15–21:01:10 (uploaded).

2026-03-13 21:20 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): I can reproduce in a staging compaction run. UI emits 'dashboard:request_snapshot' then receives 'dashboard:refresh_snapshot' with older snapshot_id. Attaching trace from query-router and websocket logs. Adding component 'retention-service' to ticket.

2026-03-13 22:10 - Engineer (Priya Nair): Noted that snapshot expiration TTL logic in snapshot-store service was recently tightened (PR #4729). The snapshot-store may be returning a fallback snapshot when the requested snapshot is absent; fallback selection logic picks last-known-good per-org, which for NovaDocs in this window is 6h. Investigating whether compaction timing and snapshot invalidation race.

2026-03-14 09:02 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer confirmed impact is reproducible during their daily compaction window; they requested an interim mitigation to prevent snapbacks during active user sessions.

2026-03-14 11:40 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Applied temporary rate-limiter on compaction heartbeat to avoid emitting snapshot-invalidated events to websocket until client idle or user session flag is cleared. Observed no snapbacks in a 1-hour canary. Planning a patch to snapshot-store fallback logic.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Reproducible in staging when retention compaction completes for high-cardinality tables.
- Root cause appears to be snapshot-store fallback behavior: when a requested snapshot_id is not found (because compaction pruned underlying index shards), snapshot-store returns a 'last-known-good' snapshot id per-org. The console websocket handler treats any 'refresh_snapshot' event as authoritative and forces the client to reapply that snapshot and reset time-range / panel-level filters to the snapshot's stored state.
- Recent change in PR #4729 tightened snapshot TTL and introduced an aggressive invalidation path that exposed the race between user-initiated queries and compaction finishing.
- Query-router evidence shows the UI issues a second fetch after the websocket 'refresh_snapshot' arrives and that second fetch includes X-Dashboard-Snapshot header for the older snapshot.
- Hypothesis: snapshot-store should not return a fallback snapshot for active interactive sessions; instead it should return a signal 'SNAPSHOT_MISSING' so console can choose to keep the user's current view and surface a warning.
- Related: linked issue SUP-271314 documented a similar retention-tied dashboard drift but under different UI code path.

Next steps proposed:
1) Implement conservative fallback: snapshot-store returns explicit "missing" code rather than replacing with last-known-good for interactive websocket flows.
2) Console websocket handler will ignore 'refresh_snapshot' events tagged as 'compaction-triggered' for active sessions and instead surface a toast to user: "Snapshot unavailable — results may be partial. Refresh to reload."
3) Add short-term compaction gating: do not issue global 'snapshot invalidated' websockets to orgs with active dashboards in last 5m.
4) Roll PR with feature-flag and canary on staging/dedicated orgs.
resolution:
Workaround / Mitigation:
- Temporary: SRE applied gating on compaction-heartbeat to avoid immediate websocket invalidation events for orgs with active dashboards; this was rolled at 2026-03-14 11:30 and mitigated immediate customer impact.
- Customer guidance: if you see a snapback, reapply the time range and refresh; we will notify when the permanent fix is deployed.

Permanent fix plan:
1) Patch snapshot-store to return explicit SNAPSHOT_MISSING code for interactive websocket queries instead of substituting last-known-good. (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/snapshot-store/pull/53)
2) Update console websocket handler to ignore compaction-triggered refresh events for sessions with recent user activity and to surface a non-blocking warning instead of forcing snapshot revert. (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/4734)
3) Add an integration test that simulates compaction during active dashboard sessions and asserts no time-range resets.
4) Canary rollout to dedicated orgs and monitor for regressions; full rollout scheduled after safety window and positive canary results.

Status: In Progress. Patch PRs created and internal code review ongoing. Estimated ETA for staged rollout: 2026-03-18 pending reviews and QA.
